### Change Classification

Three classes, decided by tooling rather than by the person proposing the change. The classification determines the entire path a change takes, which is precisely why it cannot be self-assigned.

| Class | Examples | Requires | Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Additive | New optional field, new endpoint, widened enum | Tests only | Ships freely |
| Deprecating | Field marked for removal, endpoint superseded | Named replacement and usage measurement | Sunset on zero usage |
| Breaking | Rename, removal, tightened validation, semantic change | New major version and migration plan | Dual serving then sunset |

Tightened validation is the class most often misfiled. It adds no field and removes no field, so it looks additive, but it makes previously valid stored objects invalid, which is the definition of breaking regardless of how the diff appears.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this change class observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Stored Object Compatibility

Live callers can be told to upgrade. Stored objects cannot. Five rules protect objects that were written under a version nobody is actively serving any more but which somebody will read.

| Rule | Consequence if broken |
|---|---|
| Every object stamps its schema version at write | Readers must guess the shape from content |
| Published versions are immutable | The same version means different things at different times |
| An upcast path exists from every historic version | Old objects become unreadable |
| Upcast paths are one step deep | Read cost grows with the version history |
| Upcast failure fails the read loudly | Partially interpreted objects are acted upon |

The five-year audit record is the hardest case and the right design target. If a record written under version one is still readable in its original meaning when version nine is current, every easier case is already handled.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this stored object rule observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Deprecation and Sunset Gates

A deprecation ends when nobody is using the old surface, which is a measurement, not a schedule. Four gates must all pass before a version is retired.

| Gate | Condition | Who confirms |
|---|---|---|
| Replacement | A named replacement exists and is serving | Planning Contract Owner |
| Usage | Measured usage zero for fourteen consecutive days | Planning Observability Owner |
| Stranding | Zero stored objects unreadable without the version | Planning Data Owner |
| Notice | Consumers notified and acknowledged | Planning Delivery Owner |

The stranding gate is the one that catches the case everybody forgets: usage of an interface can be zero while thousands of stored objects still require that version's reader. Retiring the interface is safe; retiring the reader is not.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this sunset gate observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operational Stories

Four story types are recorded for `Evolution and Compatibility`: a normal-path story, a failure story, a recovery story, and an audit story. Together they describe what this section looks like in operation.

**Normal path.** A new optional field is added to the plan schema. The classifier confirms it is additive, tests pass, and it ships the same afternoon with no migration, no deprecation, and no governance overhead. This is the common case and it should feel unremarkable.

**Failure.** An agent proposes renaming three fields and tightening an enum, classifying the change as additive. The schema differ classifies it as breaking and overrides the claim. The change is refused until it is resubmitted as a new major version with a migration plan covering 1,335,429 stored objects.

**Recovery.** A migration batch produces mismatches on re-read. Because migration wrote new objects and preserved originals, rollback restores the previous state in four minutes and readers revert to the prior version. No object is lost, and the defect is fixed before the next batch.

**Audit.** An auditor reconstructs the sequence from the records this section writes, confirming who acted, under which rule set version, with which evidence, and what the outcome was, without asking anyone what happened.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this operational story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Execution Stories

**Execution path.** Compatibility work reaches execution as ordinary planned work: migration batches are planned units with owners, envelopes, and completion criteria, handed off through Section 90 like any other execution, and their audit records are written under Section 98.

**Boundary note.** The execution story ends at the handoff contract. Planning publishes an execution-ready artefact and stops; the execution surface owns everything after that point and reports back only as events.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this execution story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Optimization Stories

**Optimization path.** Capping live versions at three raised short-term friction and removed a long-term failure: before the cap, one surface carried six versions and no migration had been finished in a year. After the cap, two migrations completed in a quarter because finishing one became the prerequisite for starting the next.

**Boundary note.** Optimization changes how well a candidate scores against a declared objective function; it never changes who is authorised to commit. Selection between competing commitments remains a decision and is recorded as one.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this optimization story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Recovery Stories

**Recovery path.** A nightly stranding scan reads a sample from every schema version present in storage, including a version last served three years ago. One upcast path fails on an object written in 2023. The read fails loudly, the page fires, and the path is repaired before any consumer encounters it.

**Boundary note.** Recovery restores a declared state from stored evidence; it never invents state, never edits history in place, and never resumes an action whose authorisation has expired.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this recovery story observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Operating Contract

The operating contract for `Evolution and Compatibility` is the short form of everything above, and it is what an on-call engineer reads at three in the morning.

| Clause | Commitment |
|---|---|
| Guarantee | Every accepted write satisfies the controls in this section and produces a receipt. |
| Refusal | Every refusal names a reason code and is recorded; nothing partial is stored. |
| Owner | Planning Contract Owner |
| Evidence | `compatibility record` |
| Escalation | Section owner, then the Planning Owner Council, then the Lead Repository Architect. |
| Degradation | Fail closed: refuse and record rather than proceed on an assumption. |
| Budget | Stated in the performance and latency blocks above; exceeding a budget is a signal, not an exception. |

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this contractual commitment observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### End-to-End Constitutional Procedure

The procedure below is the full constitutional path for `Evolution and Compatibility`, from request to evidence. It is the sequence auditors replay.

1. The requesting role submits the action with its inputs, its correlation identifier, and its claimed authority.
2. The contract layer validates structure, references, tenancy, and metadata completeness.
3. The section's guards evaluate in order, each producing a pass or a named refusal reason.
4. On refusal the reason is recorded, the caller is informed, and processing stops with nothing stored.
5. On pass the new version is appended, never updated in place, with a monotonic version number.
6. The receipt named by this section is written and linked to the version digest.
7. A fact is published to the event boundary for consumers that do not need to block.
8. Projections rebuild and publish their lag, making the change visible to grant-holding roles.
9. The action becomes replayable: any auditor can recompute the outcome from stored inputs alone.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this procedural step observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Constitutional Extension

Part 4 extends the planning constitution established in Part 1 Section 3 and continued by Parts 2 and 3, which together contain rules `CAT-PE-CONST-001` through `CAT-PE-CONST-077`. This section contributes exactly one new rule, continuing the catalogue from `CAT-PE-CONST-078` as the Part 3 handoff requires. It adds a final architecture obligation; it does not weaken any existing rule.

**Rule ID:** `CAT-PE-CONST-101`  
**Title:** Never-stranded objects  
**Normative statement:** The Planning Engine MUST keep every object it has ever written readable in its original meaning: stored objects MUST carry their schema version, published versions MUST be immutable, every historic version MUST have a tested upcast path, change class MUST be determined by tooling rather than by the author, migrations MUST preserve originals, and a version MUST NOT be retired while measured usage is non-zero or any stored object still requires its reader.  
**Rationale:** A planning engine produces objects with lifetimes far longer than the code that wrote them: commitments spanning years, audit records retained for a decade, plans that outlive their authors' employment. Any change discipline that considers only live callers will strand those objects, and stranding is discovered at the worst possible moment, when somebody needs the object to answer a question they cannot answer any other way.  
**Enforcement point:** Schema version stamped at write and never updated, published version snapshots compared on every release, an automated schema differ that classifies changes and overrides author claims, tested one-step upcast paths from every historic version, nightly stranding scans across all versions present in storage, migration restricted to write-new-preserve-original, and four sunset gates including a stranding gate.  
**Violation behavior:** A change misclassified as additive is refused by the differ, a read whose upcast path fails raises rather than returning a partial object, a migration attempting in-place mutation is rejected, and a sunset request fails while usage is non-zero or any stored object requires the version.  
**Validation method:** Automated tests covering a rename claimed as additive, a tightened enum, a read of an object written under the oldest supported version, an upcast path removal, an in-place migration attempt, a calendar-driven sunset request, and a sunset with zero interface usage but stored objects still requiring the reader.  
**Owner:** Planning Contract Owner  
**Related Parts 1 to 3 rules:** `CAT-PE-CONST-079` (versioned public surface), `CAT-PE-CONST-100` (reconstructable audit), and `CAT-PE-CONST-094` (governed self-change).

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this constitutional rule observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

#### CAT-PE-P4-99-C01 — Version stamping

- **Rule:** Every stored object MUST record the schema version it was written under.
- **Business test:** A reviewer confirms this holds by inspecting one real object of this section without asking anyone.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Unstamped stored objects are zero.
- **AI behavior:** The agent verifies this condition before proposing a write and reports the result in the change description.
- **Human boundary:** A human MAY waive this only with a recorded, expiring waiver from Planning Contract Owner.
- **Security assertion:** Violation widens exposure or removes an audit guarantee, so the check fails closed.
- **Performance assertion:** The check is local to the object and its direct references and stays inside the section write budget.
- **Evidence:** `compatibility record`
- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P4_99_C01`
- **Recovery:** Supply the missing element and retry, or supersede the stored version with a recorded reason.
- **Implementation test:** Automated test asserting both the accepted path and the refused path for this rule.
- **Ownership:** Planning Contract Owner
- **Constitutional assertion:** This control is binding for `Evolution and Compatibility` and MUST NOT be weakened without a superseding ADR.

#### CAT-PE-P4-99-C09 — Contain: Stranded stored objects

- **Rule:** When `stranded stored objects` is detected, the containment action MUST be version stamping plus tested upcasting from every historic version
- **Business test:** The organisation learns about this failure from a signal rather than from a customer.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Detection signal: Read failures on old objects. Containment is executed by the owning core, not by an operator following a runbook from memory.
- **AI behavior:** The agent MUST NOT suppress, retry past, or reinterpret this condition; it reports and stops.
- **Human boundary:** Planning Contract Owner is accountable for the containment action and its record.
- **Security assertion:** An uncontained failure of this kind leaves the system in a state whose authorisation properties are unknown.
- **Performance assertion:** Detection is continuous and adds a bounded per-operation cost; containment is bounded by the affected object set.
- **Evidence:** `compatibility record`
- **Failure code:** `CAT_PE_P4_99_C09`
- **Recovery:** Execute the containment action, write the recovery receipt, then re-run the section's acceptance tests before resuming.
- **Implementation test:** Failure injection test triggering the condition and asserting the declared containment, not merely the absence of a crash.
- **Ownership:** Planning Contract Owner
- **Constitutional assertion:** This control is binding for `Evolution and Compatibility` and MUST NOT be weakened without a superseding ADR.

#### CAT-PE-P4-99-C17 — Security property upheld

- **Rule:** The security property stated by this section MUST hold in the implementation, not only in the prose.
- **Business test:** The property is stated in the operating contract and is checkable against a running system.
- **Engineering enforcement:** Implementation asserts the property in an automated test and emits the corresponding signal. Property: Version negotiation is a place where an attacker will try to downgrade a boundary to an older, weaker contract. Negotiation therefore has a floor: versions below the supported minimum are refused rather than negotiated to. Deprecated versions retain their original security properties for their lifetime, and a security fix that cannot be applied additively forces an accelerated sunset with governance approval rather than a silent change to a published version.
- **AI behavior:** The agent MUST NOT trade this property away for throughput or convenience.
- **Human boundary:** Planning Contract Owner approves any deviation, recorded with an expiry.

#### CAT-PE-P4-99-C18 — Consistency property upheld

### Acceptance Tests

The acceptance tests below MUST pass before any implementation of `Evolution and Compatibility` is considered complete.

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-001`  
**Purpose:** Objects carry versions  
**Given:** A newly written plan  
**When:** It is stored  
**Then:** It carries its schema version  
**Failure condition:** The version is absent or inferred

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-002`  
**Purpose:** Versions are immutable  
**Given:** A published version  
**When:** An in-place edit is attempted  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** The published version changes

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-003`  
**Purpose:** Renames are breaking  
**Given:** A field rename claimed as additive  
**When:** The classifier runs  
**Then:** It is classified breaking and the claim overridden  
**Failure condition:** The rename ships as additive

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-004`  
**Purpose:** Tightening is breaking  
**Given:** A narrowed enum on a published version  
**When:** The classifier runs  
**Then:** It is classified breaking  
**Failure condition:** It is treated as a validation improvement

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-005`  
**Purpose:** Oldest objects remain readable  
**Given:** An object written under the oldest supported version  
**When:** It is read  
**Then:** It upcasts and reads correctly  
**Failure condition:** The read fails or misinterprets

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-006`  
**Purpose:** Upcast paths stay shallow  
**Given:** Five historic versions  
**When:** Paths are inspected  
**Then:** Each reaches current in one step  
**Failure condition:** Reads chain through intervening versions

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-007`  
**Purpose:** Failure is loud  
**Given:** A broken upcast path  
**When:** An affected object is read  
**Then:** The read fails and pages  
**Failure condition:** A partially interpreted object is returned

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-008`  
**Purpose:** Migration preserves originals  
**Given:** A migration batch  
**When:** It executes  
**Then:** New objects are written and originals retained  
**Failure condition:** Objects are mutated in place

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-009`  
**Purpose:** Migration rolls back  
**Given:** A batch producing mismatches  
**When:** Rollback runs  
**Then:** Prior state is restored from originals  
**Failure condition:** Rollback is impossible

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-010`  
**Purpose:** Sunset needs zero usage  
**Given:** A deprecated version with residual usage  
**When:** Sunset is requested  
**Then:** It is refused  
**Failure condition:** The version retires on schedule

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-011`  
**Purpose:** Sunset needs zero stranding  
**Given:** Zero interface usage but stored objects requiring the reader  
**When:** Sunset is requested  
**Then:** It is refused by the stranding gate  
**Failure condition:** Stored objects are stranded

**Test ID:** `CAT-PE-AT-S99-012`  
**Purpose:** Cap blocks proliferation  
**Given:** Three live versions on a surface  
**When:** A fourth breaking change is proposed  
**Then:** It is blocked until a migration finishes  
**Failure condition:** A fourth version is added

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this acceptance test observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### AI Memory Anchor

An agent that retains nothing else from this section retains the following. Change is free when additive, governed when not, and never permitted to make an already written object unreadable. No object the engine has ever written becomes unreadable, and no version retires while anything still needs it.

**Memory anchor ID:** `CAT-PE-MEM-S99-001`  
**Concept:** Change is free when additive, governed when not, and never permitted to make an already written object unreadable.  
**Invariant:** No object the engine has ever written becomes unreadable, and no version retires while anything still needs it.  
**Relationship:** This section protects the objects produced by every other section and is the precondition for the engine changing at all after it is load bearing.  
**Implementation implication:** Implementations MUST classify changes by tooling, stamp versions at write, and gate sunsets on measurement rather than on dates.

**Anchor:** `Evolution and Compatibility` = old objects stay readable forever, governed by Changing the engine without stranding anything it already produced, evidenced by `compatibility record`, owned by Planning Contract Owner.

### Future Evolution

`Evolution and Compatibility` evolves in three directions. First, upcast paths become generated from declarative schema diffs rather than hand-written, with the hand-written path reserved for semantic changes a diff cannot express. Second, consumer capability declarations become machine-negotiated end to end, so that a surface can report precisely which consumers block a sunset. Third, stranding scanning extends from storage into archives and exports, since an object handed to a third party is still an object the engine wrote.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this evolution path observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### 2030 to 2035 Continuities

The following properties of `Evolution and Compatibility` are expected to hold through 2035 regardless of implementation technology: role-based ownership, append-only history, evidence-backed completion, deny-by-default access, and a hard boundary against execution. Technologies, languages, and storage engines will change; these five properties are what make planning content written in 2026 still interpretable and still trustworthy in 2035. For this section specifically, the durable property is that the cost of compatibility is paid continuously and the cost of stranding is paid all at once, at the least convenient moment, by somebody who was not responsible for the change. Formats, tooling, and storage will all be replaced between 2030 and 2035; the asymmetry between those two costs will not, and it is the whole argument for the discipline described here.

**Normative application:** For `Evolution and Compatibility`, the owning implementation MUST make this continuity observable through a named contract, a policy or guard, a test or review check, and an operational signal. A prose claim without enforcement evidence is incomplete.

### Diagrams

Each diagram below is preceded by its identifier, title, purpose, audience, and reading order. Diagrams are normative where they show ordering or authority; they are illustrative where they show grouping.

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P4-S99-D001`  
**Title:** Change classification decides the path  
**Purpose:** Show why classification cannot be self-assigned.  
**Audience:** Engineers and architects  
**Reading order:** Top to bottom; the differ, not the author, decides.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PROP[change proposed<br/>author claims additive] --> DIFF[schema differ]
    DIFF --> Q1{removes or renames a field}
    Q1 -->|yes| BRK[breaking]
    Q1 -->|no| Q2{tightens validation}
    Q2 -->|yes| BRK
    Q2 -->|no| Q3{marks deprecated}
    Q3 -->|yes| DEP[deprecating]
    Q3 -->|no| ADD[additive]
    ADD --> SHIP[ships freely]
    DEP --> REPL[named replacement required]
    BRK --> NEWV[new major version plus migration plan]
    BRK --> OVR[author claim overridden and recorded]
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P4-S99-D002`  
**Title:** Reading a stored object across versions  
**Purpose:** Show one-step upcasting and loud failure.  
**Audience:** Engineers  
**Reading order:** Left to right from the stored version to the reader.

```mermaid
graph LR
    O1[object written v1.0.0] --> UP[upcast one step]
    O2[object written v1.4.0] --> UP
    O3[object written v2.6.0] --> UP
    O4[object written v3.0.0] --> RD[reader v3.0.0]
    UP --> RD
    UP -.->|path missing| FAIL[fail loudly and page]
    FAIL -.->|never| PARTIAL[partially interpreted object]
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P4-S99-D003`  
**Title:** Migration writes new and preserves originals  
**Purpose:** Show why migration is reversible by construction.  
**Audience:** Data owners  
**Reading order:** Top to bottom in time; both directions available.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PLAN as Migration plan
    participant SCAN as Storage scan
    participant WR as Writer
    participant VER as Verifier
    PLAN->>SCAN: enumerate affected objects
    SCAN-->>PLAN: 1335429 objects across 3 versions
    loop each batch of 25000
        PLAN->>WR: write new objects at v3.0.0
        WR->>WR: originals preserved untouched
        WR->>VER: sample re-read 2 percent
        alt mismatch found
            VER-->>PLAN: rollback batch
            PLAN->>WR: restore originals as authoritative
        else clean
            VER-->>PLAN: batch accepted
        end
    end
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P4-S99-D004`  
**Title:** The four sunset gates  
**Purpose:** Show that usage alone never authorises retirement.  
**Audience:** Governance and delivery  
**Reading order:** Left to right; all four must pass.

```mermaid
graph LR
    REQ[sunset requested for v1.4.0] --> G1{replacement serving}
    G1 -->|no| REF[refused]
    G1 -->|yes| G2{usage zero for 14 days}
    G2 -->|no| REF
    G2 -->|yes| G3{zero stored objects need this reader}
    G3 -->|no| REF
    G3 -->|yes| G4{consumers notified and acknowledged}
    G4 -->|no| REF
    G4 -->|yes| SUN[version retired]
    CAL[calendar date reached] -.->|not a gate| REF
```

**Diagram ID:** `CAT-PE-P4-S99-D005`  
**Title:** Version lifecycle under the cap  
**Purpose:** Show how the cap converts proliferation into finished migrations.  
**Audience:** Platform and architects  
**Reading order:** State transitions over the life of a version.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> current: published
    current --> superseded: newer major published
    superseded --> deprecated: replacement serving
    deprecated --> sunset_pending: usage reaches zero
    sunset_pending --> deprecated: stored objects still require reader
    sunset_pending --> retired: all four gates pass
    retired --> [*]
    deprecated --> at_cap: three live versions
    at_cap --> deprecated: new breaking changes blocked
    note right of at_cap: pressure to finish a migration
```

### The Append-Only Contract

Part 4 was generated under the same append-only constraint as Parts 2 and 3, applied to the whole of the preceding document rather than to a chosen prefix: the bytes of Parts 1, 2, and 3 were captured before generation began, and the finished file was required to contain those bytes as an exact prefix. This is checkable by anyone holding both files, and it was checked before the commit rather than after it.

| Clause | Commitment |
|---|---|
| Prefix identity | The first 7,630,620 bytes of the finished file are byte-identical to Parts 1, 2, and 3 as they stood before Part 4 began. |
| Inner prefix identity | The original 4,805,403-byte Part 1 and Part 2 prefix still matches its frozen digest, so both boundaries hold simultaneously. |
| No modification | No line, character, whitespace run, or line ending inside Sections 1 to 75 was altered. |
| No reordering | No earlier section was moved, renamed, merged, or split. |
| No repair | No earlier typographical, structural, or factual issue was corrected by Part 4. |
| No trailing-newline change | The trailing-newline state of the prefix was preserved exactly at the join. |
| Verification before commit | `sha256sum` over the prefix and `cmp -n` against the frozen snapshot both ran and both passed. |
| Abort on mismatch | A prefix mismatch is an abort condition, not a warning; the commit does not proceed. |

### The Ten Boundaries

Ten boundaries hold across the whole document. They are stated here in one place because they are the properties a reviewer should test first, and because a violation of any one of them is a defect regardless of which section the violating text appears in. Each is enforced by named rules in the sections listed, not by this section.

**B01 — Execution boundary**  
The engine's authority ends at the Section 27 handoff. Part 4 adds distribution, autonomy, learning, and scale, and adds no second path by which planning performs work.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 84, 90, 93, 94.

**B02 — Authority boundary**  
Trust, reputation, learned parameters, forecast confidence, and agent seniority inform routing and ranking and never grant, widen, or infer authority.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 87, 91, 92, 95.

**B03 — Commitment boundary**  
No autonomous mechanism creates, alters, or discharges a commitment. Adaptation stays inside declared envelopes; anything touching a commitment reaches a human authority.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 93, 94, 96, 97.

**B04 — Truth boundary**  
Replicas, projections, caches, and snapshots are derived. There is exactly one source of truth for any planning fact, and every derived read discloses its staleness.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 81, 82, 83.

**B05 — Integration boundary**  
Planning depends on named contracts and never on another engine's internals. A counterparty's shape is an implementation detail behind a port.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 76, 77, 78, 88, 89.

**B06 — Version boundary**  
Published versions are immutable and no object the engine ever wrote becomes unreadable. Change is additive by default and governed otherwise.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 77, 99.

**B07 — Governance boundary**  
The six gates of Section 69 remain unbypassable at every topology, and segregation of duties is enforced by mechanism rather than by policy text.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 96, 92, 94.

**B08 — Evidence boundary**  
Every consequential act is reconstructable from stored evidence by an external reviewer who was not present and asks no one.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 98, 91, 96.

**B09 — Continuity boundary**  
Degraded operation never manufactures obligations. Planning may stop; execution continues against a disclosed, timestamped snapshot until planning is provably readmitted.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Section 97.

**B10 — Documentation boundary**  
This document specifies behaviour and implements none of it. Implementation status lives in `.ai/PROJECT_STATUS.md` and is never inferred from documentation completeness.  
*Enforced by:* Sections Sections 75, 100.

### Documentation Versus Implementation Boundary

Part 4 is documentation. It specifies integration, distribution, agent fabric, learning, autonomy, governance, continuity, audit, and compatibility behaviour that does not yet exist in code. Every repository path marked `proposed` in this part is a path the implementation work must create; the `core/` tree in the repository is currently a set of empty directories, and no planning core, gateway, replicator, coordinator, agent runner, governance engine, audit service, or migration engine is running. This part is nonetheless binding: when the cores are built, they are built to this specification, and a divergence between code and this document is a defect in the code until an ADR says otherwise.

The distinction matters most in this part, because Part 4 describes enterprise behaviour in enterprise language: policies evaluate, regions fail over, audit chains verify, agents are admitted and metered, plans adapt inside envelopes, and versions retire behind four gates. None of that is happening. The present tense here is the present tense of a specification describing the behaviour a conforming implementation will exhibit, not a report of observed system behaviour. The measured figures in the receipt describe this document, not a running system. A reader assessing project status consults `.ai/PROJECT_STATUS.md`.

### Integrity

**SHA256 of the final document (this file with every digest-bearing line excluded):**  
`120e830bfe0a7abfd3a6783f19f56eaa43bd752f84904ee19642b7f17740a875`

A whole-file digest cannot contain itself, so the value above is defined precisely: it is the digest of the file with every line carrying a sixty-four character hexadecimal digest removed. That rule is stable, because the set of removed lines is the same before and after the digests are written into the file. It is re-derivable by anyone holding this file:

```text
grep -v '[0-9a-f]\{64\}' context/11_PLANNING_ENGINE.md | sha256sum
```

The same command run against `_artifacts/11_PLANNING_ENGINE_PART04.md` yields the digest of the artifact, which covers the appended region only:

**SHA256 of the Part 4 artifact (with every digest-bearing line excluded):**  
`f3920f3b95493b985628c3b0b82af41a1a8bcae3332b27fa720150281ef6bdc2`

The appended region of the target and the artifact are equal by construction: the target is produced by appending the artifact byte for byte, and the two are compared with `cmp` before commit. A difference between them is an abort condition, not a warning. The same is true of the Part 1, Part 2, and Part 3 prefix: it is compared against a read-only snapshot captured before generation, and a mismatch aborts.
